page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.3xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 12 dedicated physical cores and 12 vCPUs, with a 1.0 thread-per-core configuration. The instance is equipped with 96.0 GB of RAM, yielding a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or GPU hardware, and relies on a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The hypervisor utilized is KVM.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance divergence between single-core and multi-core operations. Single-core performance is relatively low, with Geekbench single-core scores and single-threaded gzip compression rates falling into the bottom 10% and 25% tiers respectively. However, multi-core benchmarks, such as stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and Geekbench multi-core scores, reach average levels. Memory bandwidth tests show average performance for both cached small block reads at 492.94 GB/sec and uncached large block reads at 59.2 GB/sec, though the Passmark memory score is positioned in the bottom 25% tier.

Given the 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this instance provides a memory-optimized hardware profile suitable for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high single-threaded compute performance. Appropriate workloads include database operations, as demonstrated by average Passmark database and Redis SET performance of 8.48 million operations per second, as well as multi-threaded software compilation. It is less suitable for high-throughput static web serving or large-scale LLM inference, where benchmarks show weak to poor performance. The dedicated CPU allocation offers predictable execution for multi-threaded tasks, balancing resource density against single-core limitations.
